partially_covered.missing: Organization information is still limited to address and GLN. No properties for organization name, tax ID, email, or contact person. Coverage unchanged.
Item class has only net price and quantity. No unit of measure, product code, or description properties added. Coverage unchanged.
Invoice details remain scattered; no dedicated class or property for grouping details. Coverage unchanged.

cq_coverage.details: Coverage is unchanged from the previous iteration. Most CQs are directly supported, but CQ5 (organization info), CQ8 (item detail), and CQ10 (invoice detail grouping) remain only partially covered.

issues: Some object properties (e.g., contextHasOrganizationRoleAssignment) still lack rdfs:label and rdfs:comment
No non-standard datatypes detected; all datatypes are OWL 2 compliant

strengths: Rich multi-level class hierarchy spanning EDIFACT, procurement, and validation domains
Good use of functional properties, inverses, and disjointness
Clear modeling of segment and data element structure
weaknesses: No General Class Axioms (GCAs) or equivalent class definitions for key concepts
No use of property chains or advanced OWL 2 constructs

likely_oops_pitfalls: P4: Missing annotations (labels/comments) for some properties
P7: Lack of necessary and sufficient conditions (equivalence axioms) for complex classes
reasoner_risks: Complex restrictions and disjoint unions may cause performance issues on large datasets

improvement_suggestions.suggestion: Expand organization information by adding properties for organization name, tax ID, email, and contact person to fully cover CQ5.
improvement_suggestions.expected_impact: Full CQ5 coverage and improved expressivity for procurement scenarios.

improvement_suggestions.suggestion: Add General Class Axioms (GCAs) and owl:equivalentClass definitions for key classes such as InvoiceLineItem, BuyerRole, and InvoiceMessage to enable reasoning and validation.
improvement_suggestions.expected_impact: Improved reasoning support and clearer semantics.

improvement_suggestions.suggestion: Enrich item modeling by adding properties for unit of measure, product code, and description to Item class to fully cover CQ8.
improvement_suggestions.expected_impact: Richer item detail queries and improved alignment with EN 16931-1.

improvement_suggestions.suggestion: Add grouping of invoice details as a dedicated class or property (e.g., InvoiceDetails) to better support CQ10.
Ensure all object and data properties have rdfs:label and rdfs:comment.
Consider property chains for inferring roles or relationships (e.g., buyer organization via role assignments).
improvement_suggestions.expected_impact: More powerful inferencing, though not critical for basic interoperability.

summary: No measurable progress since the last iteration. The ontology remains technically solid and well-aligned with standards, but previous improvement suggestions—especially those for organization and item detail enrichment and GCAs/equivalence axioms—were not addressed. Coverage and quality scores are unchanged, and missing annotations persist.

suggestions_ignored: Add GCAs and owl:equivalentClass for key classes
improvement_tracking.notes: No new modeling was done in this iteration; all previously identified gaps remain. The ontology is stable but stagnant.
